watchOS 27 will launch this fall as the next major update for Apple Watch, featuring a useful new capability to extend your Apple Watch's battery life: "Battery Saver Notifications."

watchOS 27 can proactively extend your Apple Watch's battery life by disabling unused features

watchOS 27 is coming soon and will bring two new apps, a useful new tap gesture, a redesigned default Home Screen layout, three health-related upgrades, and more to Apple Watch.

Another new watchOS 27 feature aims to boost your Apple Watch's battery life.

"Battery Saver Notifications" are a new type of alert you may see on your Apple Watch.

When you receive a Battery Saver Notification, it means watchOS 27 has detected features you've never used that could be disabled to save battery life.

These features include various gestures, the "Raise to Speak" function for invoking Siri, and the "Start Workout" reminder, among others.

Each of these features involves background processing that can impact battery life.

So in watchOS 27, if the system detects you've never used these features, it can automatically disable them. When this happens, the system will issue a "Battery Saver Notification" to let you know and give you the option to keep them enabled.

If you regularly use these features, you won't see this prompt. Of course, you can also disable them manually anytime in Settings if you want to save some battery.

Apple hasn't specified exactly how much extra battery life users can expect by disabling these features. But it's clear the savings are significant enough for Apple to develop this dedicated new battery-saving feature.

Do you use features like Apple Watch's "Raise to Speak," gestures, or "Start Workout" reminders? Will you keep them enabled going forward? Let us know your thoughts in the comments.
